We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline.

Structure: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl ring (second) which has a trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Actually C(=O)N c3ccccc3N: amide attached to an aniline (para? not specified). So overall three steps: maybe disconnection at sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + aniline), at amide formation (carboxylic acid + aniline), and at the α,β-unsaturated acid formation via Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). So retrosynthesis: target -> break amide to give acid (trans-CH=CH-COOH attached to phenyl) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then break unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So precursor: aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) attached to sulfonyl phenyl? Wait the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So we can disconnect the double bond to give aldehyde on that phenyl ring (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Then sulfonamide formation: sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl-SO2Cl) + aniline (c2ccc(NH2)?? Actually the sulfonamide attaches to the phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) via sulfonyl group attached to the first phenyl (p-tolyl). So we can disconnect sulfonamide to give p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl-SO2Cl) and aniline (c2ccc(NH2)?? Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the second phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the sulfonamide precursor is p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and aniline (c2ccc(NH2)cc2) which after sulfonylation gives the sulfonamide linking the two phenyls.

Thus three steps: 1) amide formation (coupling of trans-α,β-unsaturated acid with aniline). 2) Doebner modification to make the unsaturated acid from aldehyde and malonic acid. 3) sulfonamide formation between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and aniline (the phenyl bearing the unsaturated acid). However the order in forward synthesis: first sulfonamide formation, then Doebner, then amide? Actually forward: start with p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride + aniline (c2ccc(NH2)cc2) -> sulfonamide (p-tolyl-SO2-NH-Ph). Then Doebner modification on that phenyl (with aldehyde) to install α,β-unsaturated acid (maybe on the same phenyl). Then amide coupling with aniline (c3ccccc3N). But retrosynthesis we can break in reverse order: target -> break amide -> unsaturated acid + aniline; then break unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid; then break sulfonamide -> sulfonyl chloride + aniline.

We need to provide JSON with three reaction nodes. Need template IDs. We haven't retrieved template IDs. Could use generic placeholder? Must be valid IDs from catalog. We can search for templates matching these transformations.

Search for amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). Use functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, primary amines; formed: amide. Already attempted earlier gave a result with reaction_id 208284 and template. That includes retro_smarts. So we can use that template ID (maybe template_id is the reaction_id?). The result includes 'reaction_id': 208284, 'template_hash', etc. Likely template_id is the reaction_id. We'll use 208284.

Now search for Doebner modification: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. Functional groups broken: aldehydes, carboxylic acids? Actually malonic acid has two carboxylic acids, one decarboxylates. So broken: aldehyde, carboxylic acid (one). Formed: C-C double bonds (alkene) and carboxylic acid (new). Let's search.
